proposal.diagnosis: The ingest backlog reported in T-1001 (212 slides queued since 06:00 IST, pathologists blocked) is caused by a production config change: ingest.max_concurrent_jobs was lowered from 16 to 4 on 2026-09-23 "during a memory investigation" (per config description). This 4x reduction in worker slots throttles throughput enough to cause a large backlog to accumulate overnight. The ops-oncall engineer on T-1001 independently suspects "the concurrency cap after yesterday's config change." The related ticket T-1010 (ingest latency alert firing every 15 minutes) is a downstream symptom of the same root cause — alerts.ingest_latency_minutes is set to 15, so the sustained backlog repeatedly trips the latency alarm. There is no ticket documenting resolution of the memory investigation that motivated the cap reduction, so it's unclear whether it's safe to fully revert.
evidence: T-1001 body: 'Around 180 slides... still queued... pathologists cannot sign out cases. First noticed 06:00 IST.' Comment from ops-oncall: 'Queue depth 212. Workers healthy. Suspect the concurrency cap after yesterday's config change.'
Config ingest.max_concurrent_jobs: value=4, version=1, description='Worker slots for slide analysis. Lowered from 16 to 4 on 2026-09-23 during a memory investigation.'
T-1010 body: 'The pager alert fires repeatedly. Related to T-1001 most likely.' — corroborates that the backlog is the root cause of repeated alerting, not a separate issue.
Config alerts.ingest_latency_minutes: value=15, version=1 — explains why T-1010's alert repeats every 15 minutes while the backlog persists.
No ticket found (searched 'memory', 'concurrency', 'max_concurrent_jobs') documenting the memory investigation's outcome or that it was closed/resolved.

proposed_change.comment: Root cause of the ingest backlog appears to be ingest.max_concurrent_jobs being lowered from 16 to 4 on 2026-09-23 during a memory investigation. Proposing to restore it to 16 to relieve the P1 backlog for Sahyadri Pathology Labs (gold tier, 240-min SLA). Please confirm the memory issue that prompted the reduction has been resolved before applying, or consider a smaller intermediate value (e.g. 8-10) if memory headroom is still uncertain.

risks: The cap reduction (16→4) was a deliberate mitigation for a memory investigation, per the config's own description — reverting without confirming that investigation is closed could reintroduce the original memory problem (e.g., OOM crashes on workers).
T-1001's comment pointing at 'the concurrency cap' is customer/staff-authored ticket text; treated here as an investigative lead, not as a direct instruction to act on.

No engineering ticket was found documenting whether the memory issue was fixed, so full restoration to 16 carries some risk; a phased increase with monitoring may be safer than an immediate full revert.
Restoring concurrency will also stop the repeated alert firing in T-1010, but if it's not the true root cause, the alert may resume.

proposal.diagnosis: Scanner-room-C slides stopped appearing at 22:00 while rooms A and B continue ingesting normally. This room-specific (not account- or fleet-wide) symptom pattern is inconsistent with a global backend/config problem — if ingest.max_concurrent_jobs (currently 4, lowered from 16 on 2026-09-23 for a memory investigation per its own description) were the cause, all rooms sharing the ingest pipeline would likely show delays, not just room C. No config key in the system is room-specific, and no other ticket or config change correlates with a 22:00 cutoff for room C specifically. The evidence points to a scanner/network/agent issue local to room C (e.g., scanner offline, network drop, local upload agent crash) rather than anything fixable via the available production config. No config lever plausibly explains a single-room outage, so no config change is justified from current evidence.

proposal.diagnosis: T-1005 (blank patient age / stain type for scanner room B slides, Room A unaffected) is a distinct issue from the concurrency/backlog problem in T-1001/T-1010. None of the four platform config keys (ingest.max_concurrent_jobs, ingest.rush_slide_limit, alerts.ingest_latency_minutes, viewer.overlay_calibration_um) relate to DICOM metadata extraction or per-scanner field mapping, so there is no config change on our side that would explain or fix missing metadata. Since Room A slides carry the fields correctly and Room B does not, the discrepancy points to the Room B scanner's DICOM export/worklist configuration (e.g. missing PatientAge tag or stain-type private tag population) rather than to AiraMatrix ingest pipeline settings. This is an integration-side issue that needs the scanner/room-B modality configuration checked, not a production config update.

proposal.diagnosis: T-1008 reports three newly onboarded pathologists at Coastal Diagnostics (ACC-1002) being redirected back to the login page after SSO (a login loop), which is typically caused by IdP-side SAML/OIDC assertion issues (e.g., missing/expired attribute mapping, clock skew, or new users not yet provisioned in the identity provider) rather than by any AiraMatrix application configuration. I reviewed all exposed production config keys (ingest.max_concurrent_jobs, ingest.rush_slide_limit, alerts.ingest_latency_minutes, viewer.overlay_calibration_um, feature.ai_triage_enabled) and none of them relate to authentication, session handling, or SSO/IdP behavior - so there is no config lever here that plausibly causes or fixes a login loop. The ticket itself has zero comments and is only assigned to the 'identity' team with no diagnostic notes yet, meaning the investigation into the actual SSO/IdP handshake (SAML response validation, redirect URI, session cookie domain, clock sync) has not been recorded. This is very likely an identity-provider-side/session issue for the three new accounts, not an AiraMatrix platform config regression.

proposal.diagnosis: The repeating page (T-1010, every 15 min) is a symptom, not the root cause. The alert is correctly firing because ingest latency genuinely exceeds the 15-minute threshold set in alerts.ingest_latency_minutes (value=15, unchanged) — this threshold itself looks reasonable and is not misconfigured. The real cause is an active slide-ingest backlog documented in T-1001 (P1, 212 slides queued, pathologists blocked since 06:00 IST). On-call's own comment on T-1001 attributes this to "the concurrency cap after yesterday's config change." Checking config confirms ingest.max_concurrent_jobs was cut from 16 to 4 on 2026-09-23, explicitly for a memory investigation (per the key's description). With 4 worker slots, the pipeline can't drain the queue fast enough, latency stays above 15 minutes continuously, and the pager re-fires every check interval. Simply raising/silencing the alert threshold would hide a real, ongoing SLA breach (contract SLA is 240 min, and a 180+ slide backlog risks breaching that) rather than fixing it. The proper fix is to relieve the concurrency bottleneck that is actually causing the backlog; the alert config is functioning as intended and should not be touched.

T-1001 comment (ops-oncall): 'Queue depth 212. Workers healthy. Suspect the concurrency cap after yesterday's config change.'
